steps.title: Preprocess and perform differential expression
steps.instruction: Normalize raw RNA‑seq counts with upper‑quartile normalization using the EDASeq R package, remove unwanted variation with RUVSeq, then run the provided Perl differential‑expression script with the specified parameters; results are written to a temporary tab‑delimited file with Benjamini‑Hochberg adjusted p‑values.

substeps.instruction: Apply upper‑quartile normalization (Bullard et al., 2010) on the raw counts using EDASeq (R package).
Remove unwanted variation from the normalized counts using RUVSeq (R package).

Execute the DE script (example for macOS): perl CSBB-v3.0_MacOS.pl DifferentialExpression <Path_To_Counts_File> <No_of_Control_Samples> <No_of_Treatment_Samples> <Counts_Threshold_Filtering> <No_of_samples_to_filter_per_Gene> <Normalization_Type>. Use Counts_Threshold=10, No_of_samples=3, Normalization_Type=UpperQuantile (or UpperQuantile+Empirical). Example command: perl CSBB-v3.0_MacOS.pl DifferentialExpression /Path_to_Local_Git/input_data/Count Data/GSE147507/Series7.txt 3 3 10 3 UpperQuantile.
Optionally, perform DE with edgeR (GLM), DESeq2 1.30.1, or limma 3.46.0; the protocol uses the Perl script above.
The script writes results to “temporaryfile.txt” (tab‑delimited) and adjusts p‑values using the Benjamini‑Hochberg procedure.

steps.title: Generate consensus transcriptomic signature
steps.instruction: Filter each study’s DEG list by log2FC and FDR thresholds, map non‑human genes to human orthologs if needed, then run GetConsensus.R to keep genes that appear in at least two studies; the final consensus is saved as separate up‑ and down‑regulated files.

substeps.instruction: For each DEG file, keep genes with |log2FC| ≥ 0.6 (≈1.5‑fold change) and FDR‑adjusted p‑value < 0.05.
If a study uses a non‑human organism, obtain human orthologs with biomaRt 2.46.3 or manually from NCBI Homologene.
Run the consensus script: Rscript GetConsensus.R --files "DE_results1.txt,DE_results2.txt" --org_assemblies GRCh38.p13,GRCm39 --logFC 0.6 --pvalue 0.05 --k 2 --outpath 'outdir/'.
The script writes two files (up‑regulated and down‑regulated consensus genes).
In the SARS‑CoV‑2 case, the consensus contains 1,467 genes (833 up, 634 down) that are concordant in ≥2 models.

steps.title: Build interactome and cluster modules
steps.instruction: Combine the consensus genes with SARS‑CoV‑2‑human protein interactors, retrieve human PPIs from STRING v11, filter edges by confidence scores, and apply Markov clustering (MCL) with inflation 2.5 (max 100 iterations) using Cytoscape or the provided R script.

substeps.instruction: Create a combined gene list of consensus DEGs plus the SARS‑CoV‑2‑human protein interactome (Gordon et al., 2020).
Obtain human PPIs from STRING v11 either by uploading the protein list on https://string-db.org/ (export as TSV) or by downloading the full STRING dataset.

Filter the STRING edges to retain only those with combined_score ≥ 0.9 (column 13) or experimental_score ≥ 0.7 (column 10). A pre‑filtered file is provided at https://github.com/SudhirGhandikota/COVID19_secondary_analysis/tree/main/input_data/other%20data/filtered_PPI.txt.
Option A – Cytoscape: import the filtered network into Cytoscape 3.8.0, install the clusterMaker2 plugin, and run MCL with the default inflation value 2.5.

Option B – R script: Rscript MCL_Clustering.R --deg_file '../input_data/SARS-CoV2_DEGS/DEGs+PPI.txt' --PPI_file '../input_data/other data/filtered_PPI.txt' --filter 'combined_score >= 900' --inflation_value 2.5 --max_iter 100 --outpath '../input_data/other data/'.
The output contains a two‑column file (gene, MCL cluster ID).

steps.title: Enrich modules with functional annotations
steps.instruction: For each MCL cluster containing ≥5 genes, compute GO‑Biological Process, Reactome, mouse‑phenotype, cell‑type marker, GWAS, and PheGenI enrichments using the specified tools and thresholds; retain top terms for downstream network construction.

substeps.instruction: Run ToppCluster (or Metascape) on each cluster’s gene list to obtain GO‑BP, Reactome, and mouse‑phenotype enrichments.

Cell‑type marker enrichment: Rscript Marker_enrichments.R --marker_file ../input_data/Lung_Markers/lung_markers_test.txt --p_value 0.05 --logFC 0.5 --cluster_file ../input_data/SARS-CoV-2-Cons_MCL_Clusters.txt --outpath outdir --min_genes 5.

GWAS enrichment: python GWAS_enrichments.py --obo_file ../input_data/other data/efo.obo.txt --cluster_file ../input_data/SARS-CoV-2-Cons_MCL_Clusters.txt --assoc_file ../input_data/other data/gwas_catalog_v1.0.2-associations_e100_r2020-07-14.tsv --outpath outdir. (Filters edges with combined_score ≥ 0.9 or experimental_score ≥ 0.7 as above.)

PheGenI enrichment: Rscript PheGenI_enrichments.R --assoc_file ../input_data/other data/PheGenI_Associations.txt --cluster_file ../input_data/SARS-CoV-2-Cons_MCL_Clusters.txt --remove_intergenic --p_value 0.00001 --outpath outdir.
For each cluster keep the top ten terms per category (based on negative log‑p‑value) to limit network density.

steps.title: Construct feature network and detect communities
steps.instruction: Create a term‑term network linking enriched features that co‑occur in the same module, load the edge list into Gephi 0.9.2, and apply Louvain community detection with resolution 0.25 to obtain higher‑order functional complexes.

substeps.instruction: Generate a tab‑delimited file where each row lists two enriched terms (source, destination) that share at least one common MCL cluster.
Open Gephi (version 0.9.2), import the edge list as a graph.
Run the Louvain clustering algorithm (Blondel et al., 2008) with resolution set to 0.25.
Export the resulting community assignments; the SARS‑CoV‑2 analysis yielded 31 functional communities.
